title: Press / to jump to the search box
summary:
Pressing `/` anywhere on the search page focuses the search box and selects its text, the way GitHub, YouTube and most search-heavy sites behave. Nothing happens while focus is already in a form field, so typing a `/` into an address or a message still works.

| Key | Focus | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/` | Page | Search box focused, text selected |
| `/` | Input, textarea, select | Types a `/` as usual |
| `Ctrl`/`⌘`/`Alt` + `/` | Anywhere | Left to the browser |

One file changes: [FilterBar.tsx](diff:client/src/components/FilterBar.tsx).

sections.title: The keyboard listener
sections.body:
A document-level `keydown` listener is added once, when the filter bar mounts, and removed when it unmounts ([FilterBar.tsx](diff:client/src/components/FilterBar.tsx#L44-L57)).

It returns early when:

- the key is not `/`, or a modifier is held, so browser shortcuts keep working;
- the event comes from an `input`, `textarea`, `select` or `contenteditable` element, checked with `closest` so nested elements count too.

Otherwise it calls `preventDefault()` (Firefox would open quick find), focuses the input and selects its text, so a new search replaces the old one.

> [!TIP]
> The input is reached through a ref rather than a DOM query, so a second filter bar on the page could not steal focus.

sections.title: Announcing the shortcut
sections.body:
The search input gets the ref and `aria-keyshortcuts="/"` ([FilterBar.tsx](diff:client/src/components/FilterBar.tsx#L75-L80)). Screen readers read the shortcut out with the field's label, so keyboard and screen reader users can find it without a visible hint.

Checked in Chrome, Firefox and Safari: `/` from the page, from the map and from a result card; typing `/` into the search box itself and into the contact form.
